Summary: God's call command to Abram: get out of his country, kindred, and father's house to a land God would show him.
Commandment: Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee.
Application: The founding migration command of the patriarchal story: one man, one departure, with promises attached (a great nation, blessing to all families of the earth). Completed when Abram departed as commanded (Genesis 12:4); never reissued as a standing law.
Purpose: To separate Abram for the covenant people and the promised land from which blessing would reach all families of the earth (Genesis 12:2-3).
Function: One man, one departure, with promises attached. This was a one-time command, given once to Abram for a specific moment, so the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not apply to it. Its goal was to separate Abram for the covenant people and the promised land from which blessing would reach all families of the earth. The evil or restraint angle does not apply here; this was a founding migration, not a law against a recurring evil. Abram departed as commanded, and the promises went with him.
